creativeDirection: Daylight location photography in a believable rehearsal room, using one sleeve's room as the real place and another sleeve's portrait/motif as the main staged action.
scene: A worn music rehearsal room based on the softly lit room from source 1: striped wooden floorboards, plain walls, a left-side window, and framed artworks leaning against the wall. In that room, the two men from source 2 stand close together in the near ground, front-facing and properly lit, with a large handcrafted golden sun-face wall piece mounted above and behind them as the dominant object. The moment feels like a posed editorial portrait between songs, with instruments and graphic details naturally embedded in the room.

elements.element: the room itself rebuilt as a real interior with striped floorboards, left-side window light, plain walls, leaning framed artworks, and an electric guitar resting nearby
the two men from reference image 2 standing together beneath a large golden sun-face wall piece
a circular practice amp grille or wall panel with pale concentric rings and subtle circuit-like patterning in purple and grey
a basketball hoop and backboard fixed high in the upper left corner, with a neon-green net
a small jagged yellow starburst sticker or painted mark on a road case near the floor
beige, grey and monochrome sandy tones subdued into the room's materials

coverSummaries.album: Clowns and Jugglers The Songs of Syd Barrett
coverSummaries.description: A painted portrait of one long-haired man sitting cross-legged on a striped wooden floor, holding an electric guitar, with framed artworks leaning against the wall behind him and a vase of yellow flowers by a window with light streaming in from the left.
coverSummaries.people: one man seated cross-legged holding a guitar
coverSummaries.place: A softly lit room with striped floorboards, a window on the left, plain walls, leaning paintings, and a vase of flowers.

coverSummaries.description: A dense surreal collage featuring two men standing amid symbolic objects and painted marks, with a large golden sun face above them, rocky forms, flowers, hearts, birds, planets, and assorted sculptural elements layered across a blue-toned background.
coverSummaries.people: two men standing among surreal props and symbolic objects

coverSummaries.description: A stark black cover showing a glowing green skeleton reaching up to dunk a ball through a basketball hoop, with the hoop and backboard angled in from the upper left.
A black-and-white photograph of a very crowded beach packed with hundreds of people in swimwear, many waving, shielding their eyes, or looking toward the camera.
coverSummaries.people: a very large crowd of beachgoers in swimwear
coverSummaries.place: A sunlit beach densely filled with people, with sand almost completely obscured by the crowd.

coverSummaries.description: A graphic illustration of a robotic or helmeted head made of circuit-like patterns centered on a purple background with red dots and pale concentric rings.
A studio photograph of three boys in matching dark uniforms with red trim and peaked caps, standing shoulder to shoulder against a pale backdrop and smiling at the camera.
coverSummaries.people: three boys in matching uniform outfits and caps
coverSummaries.place: A plain studio-like setting with a light backdrop and strong frontal lighting casting soft shadows.

coverSummaries.description: A bold graphic cover with large slanted lettering across a red, white, and green background, plus a yellow oval badge at top left and a jagged yellow starburst at lower right.

prompt: A real interior rehearsal room photographed from a low eye-level angle in a tight two-figure portrait, based on the room from reference image 1: striped wooden floorboards, plain walls, a tall window on the left with bright midday daylight, framed artworks leaning casually against the wall, and an electric guitar resting naturally in the room. The primary subject is the two men from reference image 2, standing together in the near ground at three-quarter length, front-facing, posed and recognisable, properly lit by the room's window light and a few warm practical lamps, with their expressions and styling preserved. Above and behind them, mount a large handcrafted golden sun-face as a real wall object, dominant but integrated into the room. Add source-specific details as smaller finds: a purple and grey circular amp grille or wall panel with pale concentric rings and subtle circuit patterning from reference image 5; a basketball hoop and backboard entering from the upper left with a neon-green net recalling reference image 3; a small jagged yellow starburst sticker or painted mark on a road case near the floor from reference image 7. No other people anywhere. Photographic realism, crisp editorial music photography, clean surfaces, no text. Compose it as a cohesive single moment, not symmetrical, with the figures stacked against the room and the sun-face above them, faces sharp and clear. Midday window light from the left balanced by warm practical room lights, bright enough to read at small size. Palette of warm browns, reds, oranges, blue accents, gold, purple, and a small hit of neon green; intimate, surreal, lived-in mood. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 2 shows two men standing among surreal props and symbolic objects, and reference images 8, 9 are enlarged close-ups of those same people, one face each from left to right - take each face from its own close-up. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 1, 4, 6 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
